question: How does a SEP-31 cross-border payment move between a sending anchor and a receiving anchor, and where do SEP-38 indicative and firm quotes fit?

golden.answer: In SEP-31 the sending anchor takes the sender's funds, creates a transaction with the receiving anchor, then pays that anchor's Stellar account using the memo it was given; the receiving anchor delivers the funds to the recipient. SEP-38 supplies prices: indicative prices are estimates, while a firm quote has an id and an expiry that the SEP-31 transaction can reference.
keyFacts: In SEP-31, the sending anchor pays the receiving anchor with a Stellar payment.
The receiving anchor delivers the funds to the recipient's financial account.
SEP-38 indicative prices are non-binding estimates.
A SEP-38 firm quote has an id and an expiry.
avoid: Do NOT describe SEP-31 as an interactive flow that the end user completes in an anchor-hosted page.
golden.notes: Do not require endpoint names or status values. SEP-31 is Active and SEP-38 is Draft; do not require either status.

activation.author: gap lanes gap-1, gap-2, gap-3 (Claude Fable 5.2)

truth.notes: Spec versions read 2026-11-14: SEP-31 v3.1.0 (Active, updated 2024-11-05), SEP-38 v2.5.0 (Draft, updated 2025-02-26). SEP-31 says the receiving anchor's payout may be off or on Stellar, so the golden does not say 'off-chain'. Duplicate note: active cases q-sep-31-cross-border and q-sep-38-quotes test parts of this knowledge today, but the coverage plan merges both away (survivors q-sep6-sep24-sep31-choice and q-sep-catalog-list) and opens this slot; this proposal replaces them with one case for the leaf.

sources.quote: The Sending Anchor sends the funds to the Receiving Anchor's Stellar account (on-Stellar)
The Receiving Anchor sends funds to the Receiving Client's financial account (off/on-Stellar)
quote_id: (optional) The id returned from a SEP-38 POST /quote response.
These prices are indicative. The actual price will be calculated at conversion
expires_at: The date and time by which the anchor must receive funds from the client.
If type=firm, your response must include the id & expires_at date-time field and reserve the liquidity needed to fulfil this quote until the quote expires.
SEP-31 allows for a means by which wallets and/or exchanges interact with Stellar's existing set of send-side services.
The SEP-38 standard defines a way for anchors to provide quotes for the exchange of an off-chain asset and a different on-chain asset

corroboration.claim: In SEP-31 the sending anchor pays the receiving anchor's Stellar account with a memo from the receiving anchor, and the receiving anchor delivers the funds to the recipient's financial account.

evidence.note: Abstract steps 1 to 3 and the stellar_account_id, stellar_memo fields of the POST /transactions response.
If the Sending Anchor has sent the funds, the Receiving Anchor should change the transaction status to pending_receiver.

corroboration.claim: SEP-38 indicative prices are non-binding estimates, and a SEP-38 firm quote has an id and an expires_at that a SEP-31 transaction can reference by quote_id.

evidence.note: GET /prices and GET /price are indicative; POST /quote returns id and expires_at.
POST /transactions accepts quote_id from a SEP-38 POST /quote response.
Docs distinguish firm quotes (id, expires_at, reserved liquidity) from indicative ones.

corroboration.claim: SEP-31 has no anchor-hosted interactive user interface; customer KYC for SEP-31 goes through SEP-12.

evidence.note: The flow diagram shows SEP-10, SEP-12, SEP-31 and SEP-38 API calls between the two anchors only.
SEP-6 and SEP-31 use this protocol.

evidence: Sibling sweep: q-sep-31-cross-border, q-sep-38-quotes, q-sep6-sep24-sep31-choice, q-sep-catalog-list and q-sep-6-vs-31-misnumber-trap agree with these facts.
